{"findings":[

    "file": "packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx",

    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "TypeScript cannot narrow cacheUpdatedAt through hasCache",
    "body": "The prop `cacheUpdatedAt` is typed as `Date | null | undefined`. The variable `hasCache` is computed as `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`, but testing `hasCache` in JSX does not narrow the original `cacheUpdatedAt`. Therefore `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` still receives `Date | null | undefined`, which is a type error under strict null checks and will fail the build. Use a direct `cacheUpdatedAt && (...)` check or assign the narrowed value to a separate variable before formatting."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx",
    "line": 46,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars query",
    "body": "`deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` when deletion succeeds, unlike `disconnectMutation`, which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`. Since the connected calendars query is not invalidated after a successful cache deletion, the UI can keep showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` and continue offering the delete-cache action until some other refetch happens. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the delete mutation's success or settled handler."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts",
    "line": 174,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "Cache status includes expired cache entries",
    "body": "`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` and returns the max `updatedAt` without filtering on `expiresAt`. However `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows where `expiresAt >= now`. As a result, a credential can be shown as having live cache data, with a delete-cache action, even when all of its cache entries are expired and not actually used. Add a filter such as `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the groupBy query."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts",
    "line": 25,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "api",
    "title": "Authorization failure is thrown as a generic 500 error",
    "body": "When the credential is missing or does not belong to the current user, the handler throws `new Error(\"Credential not found or access denied\")`. An untyped `Error` from a tRPC procedure is treated as an internal server error, so clients receive a 500 for an authorization failure instead of a 401/403 or 404. Throw `TRPCError` with `UNAUTHORIZED` or `NOT_FOUND` so the API contract is correct and these expected failures are not logged as server crashes."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx",

    "severity": "low",
    "category": "doc_defect",
    "title": "Hardcoded en-US date formatting ignores user locale",
    "body": "The component calls `useLocale()` for translated labels but formats the cache timestamp with a hardcoded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(\"en-US\", ...)`. Non-English users will see US date and time conventions regardless of their locale preference. Use the locale obtained from `useLocale`/i18n when constructing the `Intl.DateTimeFormat`."
  },
  {
    "file": "scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh",
    "line": 68,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "macOS-only sed syntax fails on Linux",
    "body": "The script uses `sed -i '' -E ...`, which is BSD/macOS syntax. GNU sed, the default on Linux, treats the empty string as a file argument and fails with an error such as \"can't read '': No such file or directory\", so the script cannot update `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` on Linux. Use a portable approach such as GNU `sed -i -E` or a temp-file/`perl -pi` replacement."

findings.title: TypeScript cannot narrow cacheUpdatedAt through hasCache
findings.body: The prop `cacheUpdatedAt` is typed as `Date | null | undefined`. The variable `hasCache` is computed as `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`, but testing `hasCache` in JSX does not narrow the original `cacheUpdatedAt`. Therefore `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` still receives `Date | null | undefined`, which is a type error under strict null checks and will fail the build. Use a direct `cacheUpdatedAt && (...)` check or assign the narrowed value to a separate variable before formatting.

findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` when deletion succeeds, unlike `disconnectMutation`, which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`. Since the connected calendars query is not invalidated after a successful cache deletion, the UI can keep showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` and continue offering the delete-cache action until some other refetch happens. Invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in the delete mutation's success or settled handler.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired cache entries
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` and returns the max `updatedAt` without filtering on `expiresAt`. However `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows where `expiresAt >= now`. As a result, a credential can be shown as having live cache data, with a delete-cache action, even when all of its cache entries are expired and not actually used. Add a filter such as `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the groupBy query.

findings.title: Authorization failure is thrown as a generic 500 error
findings.body: When the credential is missing or does not belong to the current user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. An untyped `Error` from a tRPC procedure is treated as an internal server error, so clients receive a 500 for an authorization failure instead of a 401/403 or 404. Throw `TRPCError` with `UNAUTHORIZED` or `NOT_FOUND` so the API contract is correct and these expected failures are not logged as server crashes.

findings.title: Hardcoded en-US date formatting ignores user locale
findings.body: The component calls `useLocale()` for translated labels but formats the cache timestamp with a hardcoded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`. Non-English users will see US date and time conventions regardless of their locale preference. Use the locale obtained from `useLocale`/i18n when constructing the `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

findings.title: macOS-only sed syntax fails on Linux
findings.body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E ...`, which is BSD/macOS syntax. GNU sed, the default on Linux, treats the empty string as a file argument and fails with an error such as "can't read '': No such file or directory", so the script cannot update `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` on Linux. Use a portable approach such as GNU `sed -i -E` or a temp-file/`perl -pi` replacement.
